image_prompt.text: The big halfpipe and bowl complex as the park's tallest concrete structure, readable from across the whole lot
Flat concrete run-up lanes threading between the ramps so there is an obvious skating line from one feature to the next
A raised quarter-pipe deck at the park's edge composed as a view down over the bowl and the ramp field
a big halfpipe and bowl area with smooth curved concrete transitions
several quarter pipes of different sizes, angled and curved concrete faces
flat ramps with straight inclines in concrete gray
a funbox with stairs and rails set into the middle of the lot
metallic silver grind rails, cylindrical and rectangular, run beside and across the ramps
a realistic outdoor concrete-gray skatepark surface spanning roughly 100x100 studs

notes: Stage A None: the prompt describes a place and its geometry with no game type, scoring, rounds or objective, so no-genre.md was loaded and nothing else. Stage B: there is plainly a space and skaters move through it, so no SET.

Axes left at default except verticality, set to tiered: the bowl, quarter pipes of varying height, funbox and launch ramp are real elevation across the lot rather than dressing on a flat surface. Nothing overhangs (curved transitions only), so P2 was not taken.

Preset caveat: Explorable Place is defined with every axis at default, which routes P0. Name kept and all three of its options kept, but verticality was moved off default to tiered, so the route is P0 + tiered rather than the preset's P0.

The park's ramps, rails, funbox and launch ramp match no option in the loaded file and are carried as id: null image entries; the stated 100x100 stud extent is carried in text since no count field applies to a footprint.
No Universal Option applied. terrain-relief was considered and rejected: the relief here is poured concrete, not natural landform.

would have asked: Sounds like an environment showcase: one outdoor concrete lot with the halfpipe and bowl complex as the anchor you can see from anywhere, flat run-up lanes threading between the ramps, and a raised deck composed as a viewpoint over the park, plus every ramp, rail, funbox and launch ramp you listed. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: whether the ramp heights should read as real elevation across the lot (a tiered build) or as a flat slab with ramps sitting on it, and whether any bowl lip or coping actually curls past vertical, which would push the build to P2.
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space? Fencing, floodlights, benches, graffiti, or skaters in the park would all change what gets drawn.
